claim: Cerbos is an end-to-end authorization platform: open-source Cerbos PDP (stateless policy decision point with 'sub-millisecond latency' claim), Cerbos Hub control plane ('policy authoring, testing, versioning, distribution, and audit visibility'), and Cerbos Synapse enrichment layer; positioned for Zero Trust and AI-agent authorization, aimed at identity, security, product, and developer teams. Homepage claims 'Structured decision logs with policy version lineage, built in.'
notes: Compliance-ready framing lists SOC 2, SOC 3, HIPAA, ISO 27001, GDPR, FedRAMP, PCI DSS, NIS2, DORA. Deployable cloud, self-hosted, on-premise, air-gapped.

claim: CheckResources (/api/check/resources) is 'the main API entrypoint for checking permissions for a set of resources' (default limits 50 resources x 50 actions, configurable); PlanResources generates query plans; ServerInfo returns version; REST and gRPC interfaces accept identical structures; per-action decisions are EFFECT_ALLOW/EFFECT_DENY; includeMeta returns matchedPolicy, matchedScope, and effectiveDerivedRoles; every response carries cerbosCallId 'stored in the audit log for this request'.
notes: Synchronous request/response decisioning is the core product function.

claim: Cerbos PDP product page claims 'sub-millisecond policy evaluation' via stateless design, 'infinitely scalable', deployable self-hosted including 'air-gapped, high security environments', serverless, and sidecar models.
page_title: Cerbos Policy Decision Point: Open-Source Authorization Solution
notes: Latency figure is marketing; low-latency architecture (sidecar/in-process WASM) is corroborated by official deployment and embedded-PDP docs (CERBOS-020, CERBOS-043).

claim: The decision output model is binary per action: EFFECT_ALLOW or EFFECT_DENY. No third 'review/escalate' verdict exists in the API.
notes: Inference (labeled): a review-style outcome could be emulated by pairing a DENY/ALLOW with policy output values, but it is not a first-class verdict.

claim: Policy outputs: CEL output expressions evaluated when a rule activates (output.when.ruleActivated) or when its condition fails (output.when.conditionNotMet) are returned in the API response; docs: outputs are 'useful if you want to take specific actions in your application based on the triggered rules', e.g. a string explaining a working-hours denial; values can be strings, numbers, booleans, maps, lists.
notes: Reason-code-style responses are DIY via CEL; no standardized reason taxonomy is provided.

claim: Conditions are written in Common Expression Language (CEL) against principal id/roles/attributes (P), resource kind/id/attributes (R), auxData JWT claims (multiple named tokens since v0.55.0), variables, constants, globals, and runtime.effectiveDerivedRoles; standard logical/comparison operators plus in-membership; all/any/none condition blocks may be nested.
notes: Arbitrary free-form attributes are evaluable; context must be supplied by the caller (or fetched via Synapse).

claim: 'Policies are uniquely identified by the resource name and version pair.' Multiple versions of the same policy can be maintained and served simultaneously (e.g., production vs staging); the special value 'default' is the automatic fallback when no version is specified in a request.
notes: Requests can pin principal/resource policyVersion explicitly.

claim: Documented policy types: resource policies (rules for actions on a resource), principal policies (per-user overrides), derived roles (contextual roles computed at request time from base roles + attributes), role policies, exported variables, and exported constants; plus scoped policies and scope permissions. Policies are YAML/JSON files.
notes: The documented entity model is authorization-only (principal, resource, action); no campaign/entry/prize/ledger entities exist anywhere in the product.

claim: Scoped policies: hierarchical dot-notation scopes (e.g., a.b.c) evaluated most-specific-first up the chain to the base policy; two modes: SCOPE_PERMISSIONS_OVERRIDE_PARENT ('first policy to return a decision wins for each action') and SCOPE_PERMISSIONS_REQUIRE_PARENTAL_CONSENT_FOR_ALLOWS ('leaf nodes can only restrict access'). Documented use cases: multi-tenant SaaS per-tenant customization and 'regional or departmental customisations to their global access rules'. No gaps allowed in scope chains; schemas must match across a chain.
notes: Mechanically suitable for jurisdiction hierarchies (e.g., us.california); Cerbos supplies no jurisdiction/legal content.

claim: CEL condition language includes Cerbos time extensions now() ('Current time on the server. This is a Cerbos extension to CEL') and timeSince(), RFC3339 timestamp conversion, and durations (ns/us/ms/s/m/h), enabling time-window and date-based rules; policy test suites can pin 'now' for deterministic temporal testing.
notes: Temporal logic lives inside rule conditions; there is no effective-dated policy version activation (see CERBOS-042).

claim: Audit logging captures access logs (all API calls) and decision logs ('policy decisions made by the engine along with the associated context data'). Backends: local embedded KV store (queryable via Admin API, cerbosctl audit, cerbosctl decisions TUI; default retention 7 days via retentionPeriod), file (newline-delimited JSON incl. stdout/stderr with rotation), Kafka (JSON or protobuf, sync/async, TLS), and Cerbos Hub. Every API response includes cerbosCallId, 'the unique identifier under which the request was logged to the audit log'. JSONPath-based masking and metadata include/exclude filters protect sensitive fields; authorization header excluded automatically.
notes: Audit logging is available in the open-source PDP, not gated to paid tiers (Hub backend requires an account).

claim: Since v0.33.0, audit log entries contain 'store-specific metadata about the policies used to make the decision' - e.g., 'if the git store is used, the git commit hash of the policy used by the Cerbos engine is recorded in the audit log' - enabling teams to 'match access control decisions to the revision history of the policy repository during a security investigation'. The same release added the unique call ID in API responses for log correlation.
notes: Decision-to-policy-revision linkage is a documented, shipped feature.

claim: v0.51.0 added an optional requestContext field on CheckResources/PlanResources letting applications 'attach arbitrary metadata, such as correlation IDs, user session identifiers, or trace context, that flows through to audit logs'; also DeletePolicies Admin RPC with store-integrity validation ('any deletion request that would compromise policy store integrity is automatically rejected') and PurgeStoreRevisions; role policies gained optional explicit versioning.
page_title: Cerbos PDP V0.51.0: Policy Lifecycle Management, Audit Enhancements, and Scopes
notes: Official release announcement blog describing shipped PDP features.

claim: Cerbos Hub audit log collection aggregates decision logs (inputs, policies evaluated, ALLOW/DENY outcomes, rule outputs) and access logs from connected PDPs. Cloud logs are 'stored in Cerbos-managed infrastructure in the Netherlands (GCP europe-west6)' with plan-based retention. UI filters: time range, PDP ID, policy source, principal, resource kind, action, decision; policy names link to their source code. Masks (JSONPath) are applied locally: 'masked fields are removed locally at the PDP and are never transmitted to Cerbos Hub.' Exports are age-encrypted JSON Lines ('encrypted before they leave Cerbos Hub, so only you can read them'), available 7 days, and require the Owner role.
notes: Centralized, searchable decision history with role-gated export.

claim: Hub concepts: Workspaces organize users, policy stores, deployments, playgrounds ('by teams, departments, tenants'). Policy stores are 'versioned, cloud-based storage container[s] for Cerbos policies'. On each change Hub validates syntax and runs tests; on success 'a new policy bundle is built and pushed to all connected PDPs within seconds'; failed tests block deployment and the previous bundle stays active. Bundles are 'encrypted file[s] containing optimized binary representations of policies', versioned for audit and rollback, enabling tracking of 'exactly which policies were in effect at any point in time'.
notes: Test-gated automated distribution = built-in change management for policies.

claim: Hub deployments are per-environment policy pipelines ('production' or 'staging') connected to sets of PDPs, with multi-store composition 'to separate ownership, for example security team versus product team'. 'Every deployment attempt is attached to a set of immutable policy store versions, making it easy to audit exactly which policies were in effect at any given point in time and to revert any changes if needed.' A Decision points tab shows each connected PDP's ID, running build, active sessions, Cerbos version, last-seen time, and a link to its audit logs.
notes: Immutable version pinning + fleet visibility + rollback.

claim: cerbos compile validates policies pre-deployment and runs a YAML test framework: suites (_test files) with principal/resource/auxData fixtures and groups, expected effects and outputs per principal x resource x action, suite options (now, defaultPolicyVersion, defaultScope, lenientScopeSearch, globals), shared testdata directories, test filtering (--test-filter by suite/test/principal/resource/action with globs), skip flags, and tree/list/json outputs. CI integrations documented for GitHub Actions (cerbos-setup-action, cerbos-compile-action), GitLab CI, and Dagger; docs recommend 'a git hook or a CI step to run the Cerbos compiler before you push any policy changes to production'.
page_title: Validating and testing policies :: Cerbos Documentation
notes: First-class policy unit testing incl. pinned clock for temporal rules.

claim: Cerbos Hub 'automatically validates, tests, signs, and distributes every policy change, giving you a turnkey CI/CD pipeline without extra infrastructure'; pushes bundles to every connected PDP for 'fleet-wide consistency'; supports embedded decision points that 'evaluate policies locally in browsers, edge functions, and other JavaScript environments using WebAssembly'; audit streaming enabled with 'one line of configuration'; collaborative playground IDEs.
notes: Bundle signing is the documented integrity mechanism; no audit-log hash-chaining documented.

claim: Hub policy stores support five ingestion methods: git repositories ('Structured policy as code managed with pull requests and reviews'), CI/CD pipelines, Cerbos Hub SDKs, cerbosctl CLI, and browser upload; per-store scoped client credentials with usage/last-used visibility; 'automatic validation ensures policies are correctly formatted' and store-specific tests run automatically on changes.
notes: Approval gates are whatever the customer's git process enforces (e.g., required PR reviewers); no Hub-native approval workflow documented.

claim: Embedded PDPs (ePDP): the @cerbos/embedded-server WASM file 'contains only the policy evaluation engine', while '@cerbos/embedded-client' fetches policy bundles from Cerbos Hub at runtime (default 60s polling; 'The minimum interval is 10 seconds'). Runs in browsers (Vite/Webpack/Rspack), Next.js, Node.js, edge runtimes, React Native. Limitations: 'Decision logs can be captured via the onDecision callback but are not automatically sent to Cerbos Hub or other destinations'; 'The embedded runtime does not expose administrative endpoints'; bundle rules filter policies by resource/action/scope/role/version.
page_title: Embedded Policy Decision Points :: Cerbos Documentation
notes: In-process evaluation eliminates network hop; audit centralization is weaker in embedded mode (see also CERBOS-045-adjacent blog confirming logs stay local).

claim: Cerbos implements the OpenID AuthZEN interoperability specification: /.well-known/authzen-configuration metadata, /access/v1/evaluation (single) and /access/v1/evaluations (batch) endpoints, alongside its native REST and gRPC APIs.
notes: Standards-based interface reduces lock-in in both directions.

claim: PEP integrations / client SDKs are documented for JavaScript, Go, Python, Java, .NET, Rust, PHP, and Ruby.
page_title: Cerbos Authorization Platform Overview :: Cerbos Documentation
notes: Hub additionally ships SDKs for policy-store management (JS, Python, Go, Java, .NET, PHP, Rust per Hub index).

claim: Admin API operations: add/update policies (POST/PUT /admin/policy), list/filter policies by name/scope/version, get by id, delete, disable/enable, inspect ('list actions and variables covered by the policies'), schema add/list/get/delete, store reload (GET /admin/store/reload), purge revisions, and audit log retrieval (GET /admin/auditlog/list/{kind} with filters). 'Authentication is mandatory for the Admin API. Currently only basic authentication with a single admin user is supported.' Dynamic policy management requires mutable stores (SQLite3, MySQL, Postgres); blob/disk/git support reload only.
page_title: The Cerbos Admin API :: Cerbos Documentation
notes: Single-admin basic auth is a governance limitation on the self-hosted control surface (Hub is the multi-user alternative).

claim: Storage drivers: disk (watchForChanges, archive support), git (local/remote over HTTPS/SSH with updatePollInterval), blob (AWS S3, GCS, S3-compatible e.g. Minio), Cerbos Hub bundle store, SQLite3/MySQL/Postgres (dynamic stores supporting Admin API runtime updates), and overlay (base + fallback driver with circuit breaker pattern).
notes: Policies are plain YAML/JSON files in customer-controlled storage; export/portability is inherent.

claim: Cerbos Hub RBAC: organization roles Owner, Developer, Analyst, Viewer, and Member ('must be explicitly granted workspace roles in order to access a workspace'); workspace roles Owner (full control incl. member management), Developer (manage API keys, view builds), Analyst ('can view audit logs but cannot export them'), Viewer (read-only). Organization-level permissions are inherited by all workspaces except for Member.
notes: Fixed role set; no custom roles documented; page does not document SSO or policy-approval workflows.

claim: Public pricing: Open Source 'free forever'; Proof of Concept $0/month (up to 100 monthly active principals, 1 workspace, 2 developers, 2 simultaneous PDPs, '1 week of unified audit logs'); Development from $25/month (first 100 MAPs, 3 workspaces, 5 developers, 10 PDPs, '3 months of unified audit logs', uptime SLA, live chat); Production from $933/month (first 5,000 MAPs, unlimited workspaces/developers/PDPs, '1 year of unified audit logs'); Enterprise custom (SSO support, self-hosted Hub, 'custom audit log retention', 'enterprise support SLA', phone support, quarterly training).
notes: Unit metric = monthly active principals. SSO and self-hosted Hub are enterprise-only.

claim: Cerbos announced SOC 2 Type II compliance on 2024-01-09 'in accordance with the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants (AICPA) standards for SOC for Service Organizations, also known as SSAE 18'.
page_title: Cerbos Achieves SOC 2 Type II Compliance
notes: Announcement does not name the auditor or delimit scope (Hub vs company).

claim: Utility Warehouse (FTSE 250 UK multiservice utility; 814,000+ customer accounts, 45,000+ independent distributors, 200+ engineers) replaced a decaying in-house authorization system with self-hosted open-source Cerbos PDP across 4,500 internal services; quote: 'One of our favorite features is the audit logs because it allows us to understand what is happening in the black box.'
notes: Regulated FTSE 250 company citing audit capability; also evidence that large enterprises adopt the free OSS PDP without paying.

claim: 9fin (leveraged-finance data platform serving 'top investment banks, law firms, hedge funds, and asset management firms' in US/UK/EU) uses Cerbos for product packaging and feature access 'while maintaining strict compliance controls'; product packaging modifications dropped from hours to '10 minutes'; 'There was a very low bar to get going and start shipping.'
notes: Fintech customer; policy format 'helped technical and non-technical stakeholders align on requirements'.

claim: Cerbos Synapse is an enrichment and orchestration layer that 'fetches identity, resource, and relationship data from external systems to enrich authorization requests, and translates infrastructure protocols into Cerbos policy checks'. Integrations listed: IdPs (Okta, Entra ID, AWS Cognito, Auth0, LDAP, Keycloak, FusionAuth, Ping Identity, Stytch, Clerk), databases (PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, Oracle, MariaDB, Neo4j), API gateways (Envoy, Kong, Apigee, Gravitee), Kafka, Trino, Kubernetes, OPA; custom data sources/adapters 'in any language that compiles to WebAssembly'; responses mapped to policy attributes and cached within a TTL; claims 'millisecond enrichment at scale'.
notes: Newer component; docs page (docs.cerbos.dev/cerbos-hub/synapse.html) exists per search but direct fetch 404'd; GA/maturity status not confirmed. It orchestrates attribute fetching, not risk-vendor signal normalization.

claim: Observability: 'Cerbos exposes a metrics endpoint at /_cerbos/metrics that can be scraped by Prometheus'; supports OpenTelemetry protocol (OTLP) push metrics and distributed traces, configured via standard OTel environment variables; full transition from OpenCensus to OpenTelemetry completed in v0.32.
notes: Direct fetch returned 503; content corroborated via search snippets of the official docs page and the official v0.32 release blog. Confidence reduced accordingly.

claim: cerbos/cerbos on GitHub: Apache License 2.0, ~4.5k stars, written in Go; described as 'the open core, language-agnostic, scalable authorization solution'.
notes: Open-core model: OSS PDP + commercial Hub.

claim: Funding: $3.5M seed (Nov 2021, led by Crane Venture Partners; legal entity Zenauth Ltd) plus $7.5M extended seed (Apr 2023, led by OMERS Ventures); trackers report ~$11M-$15.3M total raised; founded by Emre Baran and Charith Ellawala.
page_title: Cerbos raises $7.5M for its open-source authorization platform - SiliconANGLE
notes: Corroborated by finsmes.com (2021 seed), uktechnews.info (Zenauth), tracxn.com ($11M/2 rounds; another figure $15.3M unverified). No Series A found; company is seed-stage on disclosed data.

claim: Conflict resolution is deterministic and documented: within a role, 'if any rule evaluates to EFFECT_DENY... the result is DENY' (deny-override); across multiple principal roles, an EFFECT_ALLOW from any role yields ALLOW; scoped policies add hierarchy modes (first-match-wins override-parent vs require-parental-consent restricting children to parent-permitted allows).
notes: Combined with scoped_policies.html (CERBOS-009). No numeric rule priorities; ordering semantics are structural.

claim: JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) validation of principal and resource attributes per resource policy (_schemas directory, cerbos:// $ref scheme, ignoreWhen action exclusions); enforcement 'reject' ('the effect for all actions will be set to EFFECT_DENY' on invalid requests) or 'warn'; validationErrors array returned with JSON path, message, and source.
notes: Input-contract enforcement improves evidential quality of logged decisions.

claim: PlanResources performs partial evaluation and returns one of ALWAYS_ALLOWED, ALWAYS_DENIED, or CONDITIONAL (an expression AST of operators/operands over resource attributes) so applications fetch only permitted records; official query-plan adapters exist for Prisma, Drizzle, Mongoose, Convex, LangChain/ChromaDB, and SQLAlchemy.
page_title: Filtering Database Results With Cerbos Query Plans | Cerbos
notes: Corroborated by API docs (CERBOS-002) and docs recipes (query-plan adapters section); direct using_query_plans URL 404'd.

claim: Hub playgrounds are 'fully-interactive, private development environments that provide an IDE-like experience for authoring policies' with real-time multi-user editing, drag-and-drop file import, README rendering, an Explore tab showing ALLOW/DENY per action plus 'Effective derived roles' and a permissions matrix; playgrounds can be created from an existing policy store; 'Changes made in the playground are not automatically pushed to your policy store or git repository.'
notes: Interactive what-if exploration against fixtures, not against production traffic.

claim: MCP/AI-agent authorization: agents 'send the user context, tool, and target resource' to the PDP, which returns 'an allow or deny decision' before tool execution; Cerbos provides 'a full audit trail' with 'the principal, resource, action, and result' capturing what agents do on whose behalf.
page_title: Model Context Protocol (MCP SDK) + Cerbos | Secure AI Authorization
notes: Shows the same engine applied to gating actions of non-human actors across systems - evidence of cross-product action-authorization generality.

claim: Promoted use cases: AI security, MCP server authorization, RAG access control, AI gateway authorization, agentic commerce ('Authorize every AI agent transaction before money moves'), application permissions, multi-tenant SaaS, per-tenant custom policies, dynamic policies, non-human identity authorization, enterprise organizations, product packaging ('trials, feature bundles, and custom packages'); compliance alignment claims for HIPAA, PCI DSS, GDPR.
notes: No promotions/sweepstakes/marketing-compliance use case appears anywhere on the site; regulatory positioning is generic ('compliance-ready'), not jurisdiction-content-based.

claim: Policy files declare apiVersion: api.cerbos.dev/v1; the documented resource policy format contains resource, version, scope, scopePermissions, importDerivedRoles, constants, variables, rules, and schemas fields; no metadata/annotations field (e.g., for legal citations) is shown in the documented policy format.
notes: Stable v1 policy schema; gRPC services are namespaced (v1). No formal REST deprecation-policy document located.

claim: Absence evidence: Hub user-management documentation describes roles and member administration but no in-product policy-change approval or review workflow; the documented change-control path is git pull requests and reviews (per policy-store docs) plus automated test gates.
notes: Labeled inference from feature enumeration across the Hub docs reviewed (index, concepts, policy stores, deployments, user management, audit log collection).

claim: Absence evidence: no effective-date or scheduled policy-version activation feature was found across PDP and Hub documentation; the closest mechanisms are CEL time conditions inside rules and, for embedded clients only, manual bundle activation (activateOnLoad: false + loader.activate()).
page_title: Embedded Policy Decision Points :: Cerbos Documentation
notes: Labeled inference from documentation review; policy changes take effect when distributed (seconds via Hub; poll intervals for git/blob stores).

claim: Deployment patterns documented: Kubernetes (service, sidecar, daemonset), serverless, systemd, and cloud platforms; container images distributed via ghcr.io; configuration is declarative YAML; policies live in customer-controlled stores (git/disk/blob/db).
page_title: Cerbos Authorization Platform Overview :: Cerbos Documentation
notes: Docs index enumerates the Deployment Patterns section; compile docs show ghcr.io/cerbos/cerbos images.

claim: Third-party comparisons consistently place Cerbos among AuthZed/SpiceDB, Oso, Permit.io, PlainID, OpenFGA, OPA, and Axiomatics; characterization: policy-as-code in YAML, self-hosted, RBAC/ABAC/PBAC, 'easier to use than OPA because it comes with application-focused design patterns out of the box'; relationship-graph (ReBAC) depth is where SpiceDB/OpenFGA lead instead.
page_title: Top 5 Authorization and Policy-Based Access Control (PBAC) Tools: AuthZed, Oso, Permit.io, Cerbos, and PlainID Compared
notes: Corroborated by sph.sh (OpenFGA vs SpiceDB vs Cerbos vs OPA) and a Medium 2025 comparison; used only for market positioning, not capability scoring.

claim: Embedded PDP audit logs are local-only: 'audit decision logs from Embedded PDPs can now be recorded locally and processed in real-time using the onDecision hook'; entries contain request details, principal, resource attributes, and effect; the feature works 'without relying on a centralized PDP or Cerbos Hub' and provides no built-in transmission to Hub.
page_title: Audit Logs for Cerbos Hub Embedded PDPs | Cerbos
notes: Relevant limitation for evidence-grade completeness when policies run at the edge/client.
